Africa), Great Australian Desert (Australia), Arabian Desert (Saudi Arabia), Dasht-e- Lut (Iran),
Thar Desert (Pakistan), Kalahari and Namib Deserts (South Africa), Mojave (North America).
The aridity of the hot deserts is mainly because of descending air, off-shore Trade Winds, and
presence of cold oceanic currents along the coasts.
Climate of the tropical deserts is hot and dry. In summers, average temperatures ranges between
27°C to 30°C. Summer days are extremely hot and nights are warm. Daytime temperature at
certain places rises to 52° C. Highest recorded temperature in Al-Azizia in Libya (Sahara desert)
is 57°C. In winters average temperature is 15°C. Days are not so cool whereas nights are cool or
Deserts annually receive less than 250 mm of scanty and unreliable rainfall. Average annual
rainfall in Sahara desert is 25mm. In deserts rain occurs with.violent convectional thunderstorms
